references.text: Abraham asks his servant to swear by placing his hand under his thigh, a similar action that Jacob requests of Joseph.
Jacob repeats his request to be buried in the cave of Machpelah with his fathers, expanding on the wish he expressed in 47:29.
Joseph reminds Pharaoh of the promise he made to his father to bury him in Canaan, showing the fulfillment of Jacob's request.
Joseph makes a similar request to the Israelites to take his bones out of Egypt, mirroring Jacob's request not to be buried in Egypt.
Abraham's purchase of the cave of Machpelah as a family burial site, the place where Jacob wished to be buried.
In faith, Joseph spoke of the Israelites' departure from Egypt and gave instructions concerning his bones, referring back to his promise to Jacob.
Both verses document Israel's last will and prophetic words about returning from Egypt before his death.
Both verses emphasize the patriarchs' conscious choice to be buried in Canaan to confirm their belonging to God's promise.
Both verses use identical wording about 'grace' as the key to achieving the wish of burial in the land of their fathers.
